title: AES-X230 device profile report
description: One catalogue record read against the X230 profile — the object the device page renders. For every parameter the profile defines, this says whether the catalogue can populate it, and where the value came from. It is deliberately not a conformance certificate: no microphone in this catalogue publishes an AES70 device model, so a mapped parameter means 'the catalogue knows this value', not 'the device exposes this object'. Where the two differ, `access` says so. Produced by docs/js/x230.js from Research/aes_x230_profile.json (see its `crosswalk` key) and a record matching microphone.schema.json or rf_component.schema.json.

kind.description: Which schema the record follows. It decides which half of the profile is evaluated and which is marked not applicable.

control.description: The honest caveat, computed rather than assumed: whether anything in the record suggests the device is controllable at all.

aes70_declared.description: True only if the record actually claims AES70/OCA control. Across this catalogue it is always false — the source is a specification database, not a device model.

remote_control_points.description: How many mapped parameters are reachable over a network rather than by hand.

coverage.description: Counts across parameters[], so a device can be compared with another at a glance.

applicable.description: total minus not_applicable, undefined_in_profile and runtime — the parameters this device could meaningfully answer, and the denominator of the score.

mapped_pct.description: mapped / applicable as a percentage. Null when applicable is 0.

blocks.description: Whether the device instantiates each profile block. Decided once here, and every parameter inside a block that is not instantiated is marked not-applicable — so the reasoning is stated once rather than repeated down the table.

status.description: 'unknown' where the record cannot settle it either way.

why.description: The evidence or inference behind the status, in one sentence.

parameters.description: One entry per profile parameter, in profile order.

status.description: mapped — the catalogue supplies a value. absent — the catalogue positively records the function is missing, the equivalent of the profile's own 'N' code. unknown — applicable, but nothing in the catalogue can answer it; value is null. not-applicable — the block is not instantiated. undefined-in-profile — X230 left the binding open, so there is nothing to conform to. runtime — a per-unit or user-set value that exists only on a live device; reported as null and left out of the score, since no catalogue of models could hold it.

value.description: Display-ready value, or null. Null is the point of this report, not a gap in it: it is how the model says the catalogue cannot answer.

values.description: Set here instead of `value` where the parameter is a switch with several positions — pads, patterns, low-cut frequencies.

access.description: For a mapped parameter, whether it is a real control point. 'local' is the common case here and is exactly the gap between knowing a value and being able to set it: a pad marked '(Via Switch)' is a function, not an AES70 object.

evidence.description: The record fields actually read, so any row can be traced back to data.

path.description: Dotted path into the source record.

why.description: Why the status is what it is. Required reading for anything other than 'mapped'.
